chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Bint Ilyās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say: “If a woman dies among men, and they do not find a woman to perform ghusl for her, some of the men may wash her from behind the garment, and it is recommended that he wrap a cloth around his hands.”

Thus, the proper understanding of this report is that if that man is one of her blood relatives or her husband, then it is permissible for him to perform her ghusl from behind the garments, according to what we have mentioned before. This is also indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهَا: to perform the ritual washing of her corpse
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a piece of cloth wrapped on the hands during washing
key_terms.ذَوِي أَرْحَامِهَا: her blood relatives within kinship ties
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَاءِ ٱلثَّوْبِ: from behind the garment, without direct exposed contact
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: it is recommended as a preferred legal practice

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform ghusl for a deceased woman if no woman is available?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of washing a deceased woman when no woman is available to perform the ghusl. It states that a man may wash her from behind a garment, with a cloth wrapped around his hands, and the accompanying note restricts this to a mahram relative or her husband.
